author: Russell Brand
description:
Mark Ruffalo stood at the Golden Globes and told the room he didn't really want to be there because of everything happening in the world, and Russell Brand had one response — then don't go. The performative grief of a room full of the wealthiest entertainers on earth, dressed in designer clothes, collecting trophies from each other, while gesturing at the suffering outside has never been exposed more ruthlessly than the night Ricky Gervais stood up and told them all exactly what they were. A working class man from Reading walked into the most self-congratulatory room in the world and fired a terminal shot. Russell Brand went to the Golden Globes. He went to the Oscars. He did all of it. And every single time he came away feeling gloomy, heavy, and dark. Hollywood's wokeness has always been a performance, and the only people left who still believe in it are the ones lying to themselves just to get through the door.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Laura Loomer was thrown out of a moving Uber by a driver who screamed obscenities at her for being Jewish, reported it to Uber, and nothing was done. Then when she spoke out after an Uber driver pledged allegiance to ISIS and murdered people, Uber and Lyft released a joint statement permanently banning her from both platforms, including Uber Eats. But Russell Brand stops the conversation cold and asks the question nobody else is asking — do you really think Uber cares about migrants? Do you think Facebook cares about trans people? These companies are not conducting background checks because they believe in a cause. They are not conducting background checks because it costs money. The real targets in this story are not migrant drivers. They are the technology giants who have quietly acquired the power to erase any person from public life with a single joint statement and zero accountability to anyone.
